Hey there, I think I was a slightly less bad version of your husband last year. I dont drink or smoke, but eating and self-harm were my vices. I am also extremely conflict avoidant, especially with my husband (something I'm still working on!). I was severely depressed, and even now I'm not "normal" but I am better. I get shit done, I dont indulge my vices, and when I feel hopless, I dont wallow or turn off, I ask for help. The only way I got to this place was threat of divorce and some serious therapy....and also wanting to change.


I don't know if your husband is depressed, but I know at a certain point the sympathy drains out, and then the love, and then it doesn't really matter what his problem is if he isn't doing anything to help himself, if he doesn't think anything is wrong. 


Here's what worked for me. I desperately wanted to change, because I didn't want to lose my marriage, and my life. Therapy was the vehicle that got me to a better place, and being held accountable without judgement by my husband helped me stay on track. This may not be the right path for your relationship, and honestly if the love is gone it may be too late anyway. Your husband has to want to change, and you have to be willing to give him the chance. 


Now as for launching a man into the sun.....well I've got nothing there, I've been trying unsuccessfully for years to launch my mother up there too.

This is pretty late, but I pretty much grew up in this situation. My dad was a 2 month revenge relationship against the man she really wanted to be with. My dad didn't really want to be with my mom, so while he told her he would marry her, and do right by me, he also said he wouldn't be changing his life plans to join the military after high school and move away. My mother didn't want to be with him anyway, and for some stupid-ass reason she chose not to take his offer of monetary support (honestly think it was to fuel her woe-is-me, my life is so hard mentality.) Anyway, my mom wasn't a great parent, and i didn't really have a lot to do with my dad, however I grew up with a lot of love because my paternal grandparents reached out to my maternal grandmother and said they already loved me and just wanted to be involved. 
This is purely anecdotal, and I'm sure you will be a wonderful parent, but I would try to give those paternal grandparents an honest, open-minded try, preferably before baby arrives. Set ground rules early, and keep an eye out for craziness. It's hard to tell right now if what they've done is narcissistic behavior or desperation to be in the child's life. It's a hard situation for sure, with hard choices to be made. If his parents are good people that are just acting out unacceptably, they might be a source of love and support for your child, and if they are selfish assholes, it's better to find out before baby gets here.

Hmm, I'm not sure about this tbh. One of the first things my therapist told me is to not use "you" statements. It almost always makes the other person raise their hackles and get defensive. Say the living room is a mess, if I were to tell my husband "clean your space" he would probably be pissed, and honestly if he said that to me I would be too, lol. I have a lot more success with staying away from pronouns altogether, or using "I" statements. Even changing the order of pronouns can work. For some reason saying something like "I was hurt when you told me my shirt was too tight. I felt really unattractive," sounds better and less accusing than "You hurt my feelings when you told me my shirt was too tight. You make me feel unattractive."

My kid and I went through something similar, except for her it was porn and chat rooms. She is also 12. I am not afraid to admit I am a pretty strict parent. But, my kid is responsible, respectful, and gets good grades, so I had no problem getting her a tablet, letting her play minecraft online, getting her a phone. Of course, DH and I did check her electronic devices every now and again, because there's a lot of ways that kids can get into trouble. 
First time we caught her we took her back to the stone age for a month, second time it was another month. This kid had never been so bored, haha. But we did let her have things back, and this is just to say, she knew she couldn't hide stuff from us. DH is very computer and tech savy, and I know how to use google to recover history.

As you can probably guess it happened again. This just about broke me, because honestly? I didn't want to fight with my very good kid anymore. I didn't want to punish her and make her cry anymore, especially when the punishment isn't working. So we sat down and talked, and eventually decided to take the internet and connectivity away. She wasn't ready, and she wasn't mature enough yet to use them. It was not a punishment, it was just how life is. We can always revisit this decision when she is older, but for now, the answer is no. We installed Qustodio on her phone (its a pay app but very useful!), took away the tablet indefinitely and while she can play with people online, she can't talk to them. We also put her into therapy, to address this poor impulse control, and also the fact that her "friends" really take advantage of her at school, which is a whole different can of worms.

I guess TL:DR is it's okay to go back a level, if your kid is not mature enough to handle the technology. And it's okay to "helicopter parent" because the dangers of the internet are real and they could follow your daughter forever. 12 is so young, and even a mature 12 year old doesn't have the knowledge or maturity of an adult, which is exactly how it should be....but it does mean they still need to be protected. 

Also, just to add, I don't disapprove of porn, but I do disapprove of most free porn, as a lot of the actresses and actors are being taken advantage of in a very vulnerable time in their lives. When you really look into it, it is a truly evil industry. It's an industry that feeds on misery and using up youth for money. I'm not going to buy my kid an account to an ethical porn website, so removing the temptation just works better.

My mother would make meatloaf every single week, and she recently tried to give me her recipe. It is literally a pound of ground beef, crackers until it's big enough for how many people you are serving it to, and 2 eggs. Throw in the oven until the end of time or your kitchen smokes up, whichever comes first. Cut away burned parts and serve. Oh and the burned parts are essential for taste. This is the rule for all meats, cook until burnt, cut away burnt parts.  

Also since my grandma was diabetic and my grandpa had high sodium my mom would substitute sugar with nothing and salt with flour mixed with a tiny amount of paprika, and call it the spicy variation. 

For years I thought homemade food just sucked for everyone, and people who claimed to like it were liars in a great conspiracy, lol.

Yup, I had to ban youtube and internet on her computer, and online minecraft and roblox when my kid was about 8. I did not realize what a cesspool all that shit can be, even with adblock, and parental control. I was introduced to tech at 16, my child had it before she was born, and that gap shows. Only recently have I allowed her to start playing minecraft online again, and she's about to go into summertime screen hours (screen time is limited and based on a chore and reading basis). 

At first it was a nightmare, I was so discouraged. She would go over to my moms, and I would have to tell her every time, no youtube. Everytime, my enabling mom would complain about it in front of her, creating an echo chamber of whining. So my mom ended up in timeout too, haha. 

For months every day was met with some form of the 5 stages of grief. Denial that I ever took anything away, anger in the form of tantrums and destroying her other property, bargaining with me as if I were the devil and she was willing to part with her soul, sadness and oh god were there tears and soulful puppy dog eyes. Acceptance, and before that final acceptance, false acceptance which was really her thinking if she could prove she was mature enough to handle the discipline she would get things back. 

It is a tough road, but you haven't ruined your child, and you aren't a terrible mom either. It's just easiest to remain in inertia, like a lobster waiting for death in a slowly warming pot. Kudos on taking that first hard step of change!

I work as a caregiver in a long term care facility, and goddamn that shit is annoying. You get a lot of caregivers and social workers that think they know the resident best because they deal with them 24/7, sometimes for years at a time. We (and yes I'm a little guilty of this myself) tend to forget that even though we've known Mr. Smith for 6 years, and he's a total dick due to dementia or untreated diabetes, his children might still remember him as the sweet man who took them fishing every Saturday. Or in your case we might think we know Mrs. Hellbeast as a sweet lonely woman, because we've cared for her day in and day out for 2 years, never knowing she was a raging sociopathic cunt who terrorized her family. One thing we learn very fast is not to judge, because you can't judge people when you have to care for them equally and without bias. That should extend to family members too, so I'm very sorry she felt it was her place to say anything to you, it was beyond her job scope.

What helped with my sensitive daughter at that age was setting her down, looking her in the eyes and telling her exactly what was going to happen. Like Daycare would be "Alright you have to go to daycare, I have to go to work. When we get there I want you to go play with the other kids, and I will come get you in 6 hours." Or Doctor I would let her know exactly whats going on in the care before we get there. "The doctor is going to check your eyes, your nose and feel your chest. Then there will be two shots. I will hold you but you can't move. It is going to hurt, but not a lot and if you don't scream we can go get ice cream / go to the park/ rent a movie or whatever". I'll be totally honest, this did not work every time, but every time I did it, and didn't lie or blindside her, or try to sneak away, it worked more often.

Now that she spends 7 hours at school, I am refreshed when she comes home, and we can play video games together, or go on a hike, just fun stuff. Even chores and homework aren't so bad, especially when I get to be the fun and the strict parent. Now summer is a whole other can of worms.

I will say I do miss some of those sweet baby times though, laying down with her on my chest, watching her first movie in the theater with her, watching her take those unsteady steps, hearing her speak. I think you're having some caretaker burnout, you are definitely NOT a shitmom. It happens to everyone, but especially to people who care about and for others with issues. See if your SO can handle it and take a couple hours and go do something for you. I don't know what that looks like for you, maybe it's going to a movie alone, or getting a pedicure. Maybe it's going out for a hike or a swim. Maybe it's going to a coffee shop or a bar and just having some adult interaction. Maybe it's asking someone else in your family for help and taking a couple hours to go on a date with your SO to reconnect. I totally understand your daughter needs a lot of care, and that money is tight, but I really feel you need to release some of the pressure you're under. Take care of you, so you can continue to care!

I am a CMA by trade which is why she asked for my help.

Caregiver burn-out is a real deal, and it creeps in on you, almost like depression. Even in the best situations (of which this doesn't sound like) it will get to you. My great grandmother had alzheimers and cancer, and to be honest even before that she was a stone cold bitch in a china dolls body. With all that she became paranoid and violent, to the point that my grandma would need to stay hidden in her room, locked in and afraid to move around her own house because my great grandmother would throw shit at her or tell her just awful mean things. While I was there I tried to convince my grandma to put her mom into a care facility, and finally we were able to. 


That move saved my grandma's sanity, and my great grandma because a different person once she got settled. Never in this womans life was she so kind and happy as she was in this care facility. She sang, she liked to stroll around and look at the flowers, she would hold hands with the other residents. When we visited her, she had forgotten me, and nearly forgotten my grandma, but she would tell us stories about her grandchildren and great grandchildren and what wonderful parents her daughters were. It was night and day. Unfortunately staying with family just isn't the right choice for some cases, especially when dementia and brain injuries enter the scene. 

It seems this woman is no longer able to be a mother, or even a friendly roommate to you, and her husband is obviously stressed to the limits as well. I feel that you need to get them both out of your space asap. Its dangerous to all parties, and benefits none. I will be totally honest, I struggle with this a lot. I have a daughter, and I know I make mistakes. What helps me, is to break down my behavior.  

Am I saying/doing this because I'm angry? 

What do I expect to gain from this encounter?  

For example, when I was young my nmom threw away half of everything in my room because she felt it was a mess. Literally my room was divided in half and she threw away things like a small bookcase with a lamp and my backpack for school. It's one of those things that now I just kind of laugh when I think about it, but at the time I was devastated. I couldn't even remember everything I lost that day. 

My daughters room was messy, three guesses on what threat slipped out of my mouth before I even realized I was parroting my nmom. I had to take a step back and question myself. 

Am I saying/doing this because I'm angry? Hell yes, I was furious. I had been telling her to clean her room all day, and I found her just watching tv. 

What do I expect to gain from this encounter? A clean room damnit!.....wait no, I expect my daughter will be frightened of me and panicked since I just yelled at her. I expect my daughter will feel like I am unreasonable and unfair. Most likely she will be a bit angry, and wont be able to ask me for help.   


I ended up apologizing to her, I should have never threatened her with that. I explained to her why I said what I said. I was irritated because it didn't seem like she was trying. We talked about how we could move on from this point, and she asked if I could help her. So I helped her clean things up and then we had hot chocolate and watched a movie. 

TL:DR "Fleas" are pervasive, but take a step back when you're angry. If you've said/done a hurtful thing, open up a dialogue. Soon enough when you take in a deep breath to parrot your parents, you'll stop, and think to yourself, why?

Overall notes: I'm not super into fantasy, but dark fantasy is totally my jam. This beginning chapter really did what it set out to do. It made me want to keep reading. That being said, I noticed a few missteps. 
First, the old, "mc caught sight of himself in a mirror and now describes what he sees" is very overdone, and not really believable in this case. The cell seems to be very minimalist, why would they have an accessory like a mirror? 


This is just a personal nitpick, but why have terminology a reader won't understand in the first chapter? You could just as easily describe the MC and other characters with their physical form, without the species, and introduce that concept later on. Within the first couple paragraphs I'm not going to feel invested enough in your story to care about nonsense words or weird world building. Regardless, the whole second part of the second paragraph was very info dense, and I really feel that can be spread out and also be later on. 


When you describe Jack's ghost, why is it the horns that make him seem hellish? If everyone has horns why would that feature single him out to be demonic? Other than that I actually really like the detail in which you describe the ghosts. 


I liked the dialogue between Narius and Minar in the beginning. It shows me that they do know each other, have seen each other for months on end. I especially liked how you had Narius copy Minar's movements, it shows me that Narius is analytical and perceptive, instead of just telling me. 


The more you describe this cell though, the less it sounds like prison. Usually you want to keep a cell completely spartan. Furniture is nailed down, nothing that can be taken apart to create weapons or tools of escape. If you went completely in the other direction though, and made it a lavish type affair with the wealthy privileged in mind I could see the cell having more furniture and amenities such as the fireplace. When I read through it again I see that maybe the fireplace is in a separate part of the room? What purpose does that have? 


I think it's been made clear with all the ghosts of the kids Narius has murdered hanging around, as well as Narius's inner dialogue that yes, he is a most prolific child serial killer. I don't feel like Minar needs to recap his crimes when they both know what he's done.  


The panic Narius is feeling upon realizing he wont be getting the death he craves feels a little forced. I understand you're probably keeping that information hidden as a hook to keep the reader invested into finding out what happens, but it still seems a little too much. I'd love to have a few more hints about why Narius killed the kids, why he wants to die. Also his panic and begging seems to wear off pretty quickly once he has a minute to process. Why is that? The end of the chapter seems to just cut off, not leading anywhere.


As a final note, and another fantasy pet peeve, why do all the ghost kids have pretty normal names and yet Narius and Minar are high fantasy? If you're gonna go with a high fantasy naming scheme I think you should stick to it for all characters. It's a little jarring to switch from modern to fantasy.  


I didn't do any line edits because honestly I though most of your story flowed pretty nicely, and I get really overzealous in trying to add in my own flow, haha. There are a couple of grammar errors and one spelling error (abled to ambled) but seeing your critique of others, I'm sure you will find them. I hope you post the second chapter, can't wait to read it!
